rounds.q: How many minutes does the average shower last?
rounds.why: Showers add up to nearly 17% of all the water used inside a home.
rounds.src: US EPA WaterSense at Work, Section 3.4 (2023, citing 2016 Water Research Foundation study) and WaterSense Showerheads page (17% share)
rounds.fun: Eight minutes of shower time, and nearly 17% of a home's indoor water.

rounds.q: Brush 2 minutes, twice a day. How many hours of brushing is that a year?
rounds.why: It adds up to 1,460 minutes, or 24.3 hours. Dentists also say to swap brushes every 3 to 4 months.
rounds.fun: Two minutes, twice a day, adds up to about one whole day of brushing a year!

rounds.q: How many gallons of water does one American use at home each day?
rounds.why: Just turning off the tap while you brush your teeth can save 8 gallons a day.
rounds.src: US EPA WaterSense, Statistics and Facts (current page)
rounds.fun: 82 gallons a day, and turning off the tap while brushing can save 8 of them.

rounds.q: What year was packaged toilet paper first sold in the US?
rounds.why: It came as packages of flat sheets. The idea of a perforated roll was not patented until 1871.
rounds.src: Hagley Museum and Library, Toilet Paper: The Great Debate (research library article)
rounds.fun: In 1857 it came as flat sheets. The perforated roll idea was not patented until 1871!

rounds.q: A faucet drips once a second. About how many gallons does it waste in a year?
rounds.why: That is enough water for more than 180 showers.
rounds.src: US EPA WaterSense, Fix a Leak Week (current page)
rounds.fun: One tiny drip a second adds up to more than 180 showers a year. Drip, drip, drip!
